- When sentiment is predominantly positive (≥ 1.0) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after recent spikes.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -1.0) or mixed, model often underestimates; adjust upward, particularly if price has recently fallen.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp upward moves in history — cap forecast peaks at 1–2% below recent high if sentiment is bullish.
- If sentiment turns negative mid-horizon, model often fails to correct downward — apply downward bias starting from day 10–15 of forecast horizon.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is > 1.5σ above recent 10-day average, reduce by 10–20% unless sentiment strongly supports.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment swings — smooth out abrupt changes, especially if sentiment shifts within 5 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “1.0” followed by “-1.0”, model often fails to anticipate reversal — adjust downward 5–10% in next 5–7 days.
